acceptance: The gate accepts an execution_engine argument (CLI and Make target) and builds the polars-df adapter with it; undeclared values fail through the core validator
A test shows the gate's collects carry the requested engine argument
Existing gate behaviour and output are unchanged when no engine is given
PR merged through the normal flow
context: Decision gate: start after core-exec-polars-cli-mcp-adoption. Guardrails: shared core-exec guardrails (see core-exec-d0-vocabulary-adr context); never install non-lock Polars in the primary clone.
description: build_production_contexts (benchbox/core/equivalence/cross_surface.py) constructs each adapter with no options, so the gate always runs polars-df with the default engine. The only lever today is POLARS_ENGINE_AFFINITY, which changes the engine from Polars 1.31.0 on (probed 2026-10-08: the streaming engine's polars-stream log lines appear only with it set to streaming) and has no effect on 1.0.0, 1.12.0 and 1.22.0. After core-exec-polars-cli-mcp-adoption, let the gate take an execution_engine argument and pass it to the adapter, so the check uses the same core setting and code path as `benchbox run --execution-engine ...` and fails closed through resolve_requested on platforms or versions that cannot honour it.
